title: Empty signature images are rejected on any background
detail: The background of a signature image is now the dominant opaque colour of its border (within a small tolerance) instead of four identical corners, so an opaque blank image with one differing corner pixel no longer passes as signed. A `linkSecret` of only whitespace is refused when `authorizeSubject` is set. The tenant-scoped subject of the signing link is available as `tenantScopedSubject`, `parseTenantScopedSubject` and `peekTenantScopedSubject` in `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/shared/tenant-scoped-subject`.

title: List cursor of subject-scoped users is sealed
detail: The request list returned the plain cursor of the last base page, which could name a request of a foreign subject. Scoped users now get an encrypted cursor bound to their user and tenant, a plain or foreign cursor is answered with access denied, and `authorizeSubject` now requires a non-empty `linkSecret` because the cursor key is derived from it. A scoped user asking for `limit: 0` is refused like `offset`.

title: Unrecoverable finalisation ends in status failed
detail: A request whose original PDF changed or went missing, or whose signature image is missing, used to stay `all-signed` forever while the sweep warned every five minutes. It now ends in the status `failed` with the event `signature:event:failed` and a reason (`document-changed` or `signature-image-missing`). Renderer outages and storage errors still retry on the next run.

title: Empty signatures are rejected on every background
detail: The ink check treats an image as having a solid background only when all four corners are opaque and identical; a lone opaque pixel no longer counts the whole image as ink, and signer emails must be valid addresses.

title: Subject check for the signature feature and a readable-file check on requests
detail: `createSignatureFeature({ ..., authorizeSubject, unscopedRoles })`: `authorizeSubject(ctx, user, { subjectType, subjectId })` runs for `request`, `cancel`, `issue-link`, `revoke-link`, `sign-in-person` and the queries, except for users holding a role of `unscopedRoles`; `false` answers like a missing record (not found, `null` or an empty page). `signatureRequest:list` keeps only the rows of allowed subjects for a scoped user and reads up to ten base pages to fill one answer (no 403; an answer can still hold fewer rows than `limit`, and it has no `total`); screens and nav stay at `access`. A scoped user must pass a `requestId` eq filter to `signatureSigner:list`, otherwise the query answers 403. `request` now also checks that the caller may read the document through the same decision as GET /files/:id; a file that is unknown or not readable answers `document_not_a_pdf`. `SIGNATURE_INVALID_LINK_REASON` is exported from `signature/static-sign`.
migration: Apps that request a signature on a file the caller cannot open through GET /files/:id bind it to a record the caller can read first. Apps with authorizeSubject pass a requestId eq filter to signatureSigner:list and do not rely on `total` of signatureRequest:list for scoped users.

title: Signature requests with in-person and link signing
detail: `createSignatureFeature({ retention, linkSecret, renderHtmlToPdf, deliverLink, signaturePageUrl })` adds the entities `signatureRequest` and `signatureSigner`, the handlers `request`, `sign-in-person`, `issue-link` (sends the link through `deliverLink(ctx, { signerId, url, ..., issuedBy })` inside its own transaction, so the app can dispatch its mail write and pick the issuer's mailbox; it never returns the token), `revoke-link`, `cancel` and the anonymous, rate-limited `open-by-link`, `sign-by-link`, `decline-by-link`. Links carry a row-bound grant in the URL fragment (14 days, 20 opens, single-use signing, one answer for every rejection). The last signature sets the request to `all-signed`; the `signature:job:sweep` cron renders the signature page through the injected print function, appends it with pdf-lib and completes the request; the events `completed`, `declined` and `expired` report the outcome. The subpaths `./signature/web` (`SignaturePad`) and `./signature/static-sign` (no React) ship the signature field.
migration: The feature adds the tables `read_signature_requests` and `read_signature_signers`; apps that mount it run the schema pipeline migration.

title: Access rule option for the signature feature
detail: `createSignatureFeature({ ..., access })` replaces the default `{ roles: ["TenantAdmin", "TenantMember"] }` on the signed-in handlers, queries, screens and nav, like `createLedgerFeature({ access })`. Without it, nested `ctx.dispatch` calls fail for users that only hold an app-specific role.
